prompt: A game character faces $300^\circ$, measured counter-clockwise from due east. Which quadrant is that facing direction in? Answer with the quadrant number.
hint: The quadrant boundaries are $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$, $270^\circ$ and $360^\circ$. Which two does $300^\circ$ sit between?

hints.text: The quadrant boundaries are $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$, $270^\circ$ and $360^\circ$. Which two does $300^\circ$ sit between?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $200^\circ$ first: it sits between $180^\circ$ and $270^\circ$, so it is in Quadrant $3$. Now do the same sorting for $300^\circ$.
$300^\circ$ is between $270^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ — the bottom-right slice.
Bottom-right is Quadrant $4$, so the answer is $4$.

explanation: Quadrants are counted counter-clockwise from due east: Q1 is $0^\circ$–$90^\circ$, Q2 is $90^\circ$–$180^\circ$, Q3 is $180^\circ$–$270^\circ$, Q4 is $270^\circ$–$360^\circ$.
So the character faces into Quadrant $4$ — down and to the right. There $\cos$ is positive and $\sin$ is negative.

alternativeExplanations.title: Back up from a full turn
steps: A full turn is 360°. Facing 300° is the same as being 60° short of all the way around.
Sixty degrees short of due east means aimed slightly downward and to the right — the bottom-right corner, Quadrant 4.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the signs of the point
steps: At 300° the character is right of centre and below it, so the point is (positive, negative).
Across positive with up negative only happens in Quadrant 4.
